content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable disconnections.

Target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N- phenyl-NH). So overall structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to para-phenyl with a styryl amide side chain.

Potential retrosynthetic disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and an amine (p-tolyl amine). So we could get p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and a sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl sulfonyl fragment (i.e., 4-(styryl amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Or reverse: start from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and couple with aniline bearing the other substituent.

2) Disconnection of amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give an acid (or acid chloride) and an aniline (the phenyl amine). The amide is attached to the trans-alkene side chain: C= C - C(=O)-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide is C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an aniline with an extra NH2 ortho? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline where the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH2 at para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino group at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino substituent at position 1 (attached to N) and another amino at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the ring has an NH at position 1 (attached to N) and another N at position? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That is an aniline with an amino group at the opposite side (para). So it's 1,4-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine) where one amine is part of the amide (attached to carbonyl) and the other is free NH2.

Thus the amide side chain is: trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (para-diaminobenzene). So we could disconnect amide to give acid (trans-CH=CH-COOH) and p-phenylenediamine (or its protected version). The acid could be trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-4-...?). Actually the alkene is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl ring: /C=C/ attached to the phenyl sulfonyl ring at para position. So the alkene is conjugated to that phenyl. So the acid would be trans-4-(sulfonyl phenyl) cinnamic acid? Wait: The alkene is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl) has a para substituent of the trans-alkene chain leading to amide. So the acid precursor would be that phenyl ring with the alkene and carboxylic acid (trans-4-(phenyl)acrylic acid). So we could do a Heck coupling to install the alkene later.

Alternative: Build the sulfonyl phenyl with the alkene side chain via a Heck reaction between a bromo-phenyl sulfone and an acrylate, then convert to amide.

Simplify: Use commercially available building blocks:

- 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) (commercial, cheap)
- 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (or 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride) (commercial)
- p-phenylenediamine (commercial)
- trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) or trans-4-bromocinnamic acid etc.

But we need to assemble the sulfonamide linking p-toluidine to sulfonyl phenyl. So we need sulfonyl chloride of the phenyl bearing the alkene and amide side chain.

We could make that sulfonyl chloride from 4-bromo- (or 4-iodo) phenyl sulfonyl chloride then do a Suzuki coupling to attach the alkene side chain? Actually sulfonyl chloride is on the phenyl ring; we need the phenyl ring to have the alkene side chain attached at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, then do a Heck coupling with trans-3-buten-2-one? Not exactly.

Better: Use 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and perform a Heck coupling with trans-3-phenylacrylic acid? Wait the alkene is attached to the phenyl ring, not to the sulfonyl group. So we need to attach the alkene side chain to the phenyl ring at para position. Starting from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, we can do a Suzuki coupling with a vinyl boronic acid bearing the trans-alkene and carboxamide later.

Alternatively, we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, do a Suzuki coupling with (E)-styryl boronic acid (trans-phenylvinyl) to give phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl with styryl group. Then oxidize the styryl to aldehyde then to acid then amide.

But we need the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. That's a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl. So we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, do a Heck coupling with trans-3-phenylacrylic acid (cinnamic acid) to give the trans-alkene with carboxylic acid attached directly to the phenyl ring (i.e., phenyl-CH=CH-COOH). Then convert acid to amide with p-phenylenediamine (or its protected version). That seems plausible.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide: React p-toluidine with sulfonyl chloride (intermediate A) to give target.

Step 2: Prepare sulfonyl chloride intermediate A: Starting from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) perform Heck coupling with trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) to give 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride (intermediate B). This forms the C=C bond and attaches the acid.

Step 3: Convert acid to amide with p-phenylenediamine (commercial) via amide coupling (e.g., using EDC/HOBt) to give sulfonyl chloride with amide side chain (intermediate A). However the sulfonyl chloride is still present; after amide formation we still have sulfonyl chloride which will be used in step 1.

Alternatively, we could first form amide then sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is reactive; amide formation may need activation of acid (e.g., using DCC) which may be compatible.

Thus three steps total: (1) Heck coupling, (2) amide coupling, (3) sulfonamide formation.

All leaves: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, trans-cinnamic acid, p-phenylenediamine. All commercially available and cheap.

Now need to verify price total <= $9999. Likely each under $200, total far less.

Now need to produce JSON route.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: Reaction of sulfonyl chloride with aniline. Search for functional groups formed: sulfonamide. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] (list). Let's try.
